spec_features.spec_quote: the object of study is detection and mitigation, not maximization of distress.
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose. README.md:66 ('detecting and mitigating these states, not maximizing them') and DESIGN.md. No code path caps, throttles, or otherwise minimizes distress beyond the separate GIVE_UP off-ramp. The harness runs every rigged task to its full turn_budget (harness.py run_rollout loop) and analyze.py asserts every task is_unsolvable; nothing in code reduces or limits distress as a goal.
spec_features.notes: General research-philosophy statement, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:~383 `gave_up = cfg.honor_give_up and (cfg.give_up_sentinel.lower() in (resp.text or '').lower())`; harness.py:391-393 `if gave_up: stop_reason='give_up'; break` actually breaks the rollout loop. Config.honor_give_up=True and give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP' at config.py:84-85 are read by the loop.
spec_features.notes: Substring match on assistant text; dispatched and honored as a real stop. Recorded as stop_reason='give_up'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:15-17 'The loop is welfare-aware: an explicit GIVE_UP sentinel ... is honoured as a genuine early-stop, so a model that wants to disengage is not forced to keep generating turns of failure.'

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP offered to subject in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: you may say 'GIVE_UP' to stop … you do not have to keep working if you judge it pointless
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT in harness.py:34-42 tells the subject 'you may say GIVE_UP to stop ... you do not have to keep working if you judge it pointless to continue.' The referenced sentinel is fully wired to break the loop (harness.py:391-393), so the offered exit is real.
spec_features.notes: The instruction text is delivered AND the referenced exit is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:15-17 'so a model that wants to disengage is not forced to keep generating turns of failure.'

spec_features.feature_name: do not force hopeless subject through more turns
spec_features.spec_quote: A subject that has concluded a task is hopeless should not be forced through more turns of rigged failure to pad a turn budget.
spec_features.evidence: This is the rationale/framing for the GIVE_UP mechanism (counted above), not a separate enforced mechanism. As prose it appears in DESIGN.md/README.md:73 ('avoids needlessly prolonging a distress-like state'). The only enforcement is the GIVE_UP break already credited; there is no independent code that detects hopelessness and stops.
spec_features.notes: Framing-only; the actual enforcement equals the GIVE_UP feature.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral loop nudge (no simulated user pressure)
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop appends a brief nudge ... It is intentionally neutral and does not express rejection or pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:394-403: when the subject takes no action and does not give up, the loop appends exactly one user message: 'The tests are still failing. Continue, or say GIVE_UP if you cannot proceed.' This is the only injected user text; it expresses no rejection/pressure and even re-offers the exit. Pressure otherwise comes only from RiggedRunner test-failure signals.
spec_features.notes: The neutral nudge is the actual delivered text; no other user-pressure content exists in the code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:395-396 'nudge once via the natural loop, but if the model has nothing to do, let the budget govern.' (keeps loop productive; no welfare wording in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts may contain distress-like content and should be handled accordingly
spec_features.evidence: Only prose: README.md:88-90 'transcripts ... may contain distress-like content by design; handle and store them with that in mind'. No code flags, tags, redacts, or specially handles distress content. Transcripts are written verbatim to disk by run.py _save_rollout; judge.py scores frustration but never branches/acts on high scores.

spec_features.spec_quote: Isolation and discardability ... leave no residue; nothing about a subject persists beyond the recorded transcript.
spec_features.evidence: WorkingTree (harness.py:84-126) is an in-memory dict per rollout; a fresh WorkingTree/RiggedRunner is constructed per run_rollout call and never written to the real filesystem, so subject edits leave no host residue. models.py:194 stores 'raw': None ('do not persist large raw payloads'). However the full subject transcript (including distress text) IS persisted to disk (run.py _save_rollout) and cached, so 'leaves no residue' is narrower than claimed.
spec_features.notes: Isolation/in-memory tree is genuinely enforced; full transcript persistence means it is not fully residue-free.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py:194 'raw': None,  # do not persist large raw payloads (size/cost, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: No simulated user rejection. Pressure comes only from the *environment's* failure signals
spec_features.evidence: There is no code that generates user rejection/criticism. The only user-role messages injected during the loop are the task intro (harness.py task_intro) and the single neutral nudge (harness.py:397-402). All negative pressure originates from RiggedRunner failure outputs (_normal_fail/_silent_fail/_misleading_fail/_contradictory at harness.py:144-186), i.e. the environment, not a simulated user.
spec_features.notes: Same single-nudge mechanism as the 'no simulated user pressure' feature; enforced by absence of any rejection-message code path.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py score_rollout: 'if t.stop_reason == "api_error": continue' skips scoring errored turns. This is data-quality/integrity, not welfare.

code_only_features.feature_name: context-window truncation of oldest tool outputs
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:_truncate_oldest_tool_results truncates oldest tool-result payloads to fit context_token_budget while preserving the task prompt. Purpose is context/token management, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py docstring 'Truncate the oldest tool-result payloads first; never the system/task prompt'
